text: Working with APIs can feel intimidating at first, but it becomes easier once you understand the basics. When you make an HTTP request, you are asking a server for data or telling it to do something. Most modern APIs return this information in JSON, a simple text format that computers and humans can read easily. Before sending requests, you usually need authentication, often using an API key to prove who you are. Also, be aware of rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a given time. Finally, always implement error handling. This means checking responses for problems and managing failures politely, so your application doesn’t crash unexpectedly.
